newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM plans privatisation of key utilities.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM plans privatisation of key utilities.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said he plans to further privatise three key state-run utilities in 1997 to raise funds to help reduce the current account deficit.

Chavalit told the Bangkok Post in an interview published on Monday that he would consider selling off parts of the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT), the Telephone Organisation of Thailand (TOT) and the Communications Authority of Thailand (CAT).

The three utilities have in recent years granted concessions to private operators to undertake new business but previous government plans to sell off existing operations have been vigorously opposed by utility workers.
Chavalit said the three state enterprises post a combined 30 billion baht ($1.2 billion) annual profit.
The Bank of Thailand last week projected that the Thai current account deficit will narrow to 7.9 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 from a six-year high of 8.2 percent this year.
Chavalit indicated that private investors may be invited to handle at least one third of TOT's plan to lay an additional six million phone lines in Thailand.
The prime minister said private bidders may be permitted to operate hydro-electric dams which are being run by EGAT.
Chavalit did not specify which parts of CAT would be farmed out to private investors.
